newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares maintain bullrun in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares maintain bullrun in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares maintained their bullrun in active trade on Thursday with local institutional investors the main players, brokers said.
The key industrial index jumped 76.17 points up to close at 10,706.93 and brokers said they expected the market to continue firm on Friday.
"Institutional investors are pushing up prices. Local institutions are the main drivers of the market right now and we expect the market to continue strong," one broker said.

Merchant banker FMB , which last week announced plans to merge with newcomer in the merchant banking business Heritage Investment Bank, led the day's winners, soaring 700 cents to 5,000 while electronics group Apex rose 50 cents to 300.
Finance group Finhold jumped 45 cents up to 510, Alloys firmed 35 cents to 275, sugar refinery ZSR ZSR.ZI at 1,630, seed manufacturer Seedco at 390 and bankers Barclays at 3,380 all gained 30 cents.
Merchant bankers NMB, sugar producer Hippo and winery Afdis each put on 25 cents to 3,350, 1,700 and 475 respectively.
In minings, Falgold traded five cents up at 70 and the mining index closed 4.85 points higher at 871.42.
